title: Consistent Markings for Segregating Paths along Park Connector Network
what_it_is: Consistent Markings for Segregating Paths along Park Connector Network

sections.label: NParks revised PCN typology
sections.summary: NParks has implemented the revised typology and lane markings on continuous PCN stretches, considering path width and human traffic.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: NParks has consistently implemented this revised typology on continuous stretches of the PCN, taking into consideration factors such as the width of the path and the human traffic in the area.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: As part of the revised typology, NParks has also implemented revised lane markings to enhance the user experience and encourage safe and considerate use of the PCN.

sections.label: Next phase PCN rollout
sections.summary: NParks will roll out the revised typology for more park connectors, then engage stakeholders and assess feasibility for more.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: In the next phase, NParks will roll out the revised PCN typology for more park connectors, incorporating the feedback received so far.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: Thereafter, NParks will engage stakeholders again and assess the feasibility to implement the revised typology for more park connectors.

sections.label: Phase 1 pilot surveys
sections.summary: Phase 1 was completed in the third quarter of 2023, with surveys of Friends of the PCN and stakeholders.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: If Members realise, we have this pilot, we do it in two phases.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: We just completed Phase 1 and when we completed Phase 1 in the third quarter of 2023, we did surveys with the Friends of the PCN and the different stakeholders in the spirit of understanding that it takes time to improve human behaviour, but also to see how our infrastructure meets the needs of the people.

sections.label: Phase 2 feedback and markings
sections.summary: Phase 2 will use Phase 1 feedback and introduce more markings at smaller intervals at PCN start and end.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: When we embark on the Phase 2, we will take the feedback and comments we have heard from Phase 1 and then we will see how we can navigate this further.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: We will introduce more markings, especially at the start of the PCN and at the end, and we will make these at smaller intervals.

sections.label: Sengkang Riverside Park markings question
sections.summary: A Member asks if NParks will commit to PCN markings with colour demarcations for pedestrians versus non-pedestrians.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Like him, I use the Sengkang Riverside Park along the path that follows the Punggol River, and there, the confusion is not so much that users do not keep left, but they do not know whether to keep left on the path for pedestrians or to keep left in general along the broad path.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: So, along those lines, I am wondering if NParks will commit for the PCN to have markings with colour demarcations for both pedestrians versus non-pedestrians.
